radiation_hardness: high (metal/ceramic), but RIEMF & insulation drift on long DC integration
survivability_reasoning: Deployed on every tokamak and radiation-hard as hardware, BUT the documented reactor problem is radiation-induced EMF (RIEMF) and insulation degradation causing drift on the long DC integration equilibrium needs; ITER mitigates with in-vessel steady-state (Hall/continuous) sensors. Incumbent this quantum survey must beat, not replace.

dynamic_range: limited absolute; large slew via flux-locked loop
radiation_hardness: low: Josephson junctions & superconductor degrade under neutron/gamma dose
survivability_reasoning: Most sensitive field sensor and commercially deployed (MEG, geophysics), but requires a cryostat, a superconducting element and mu-metal shielding, all of which are incompatible with in-vessel neutron/gamma dose and the tokamak's Tesla-scale stray field. Lab-ideal sensitivity is not environmental qualification.

radiation_hardness: low-moderate: vapor-cell glass darkening, laser/optics degradation
survivability_reasoning: Record sub-fT sensitivity (160 aT/rtHz), but the SERF regime physically REQUIRES a near-zero ambient field (<~50 nT); a tokamak operates at ~1-10 T, which destroys the regime outright. Intrinsic SERF bandwidth ~100 Hz is also below the ~kHz control need. Disqualified by physics, not just dose.

dynamic_range: wide; single NV operates to several T
radiation_hardness: high: diamond host is radiation-hard; NV created BY irradiation
survivability_reasoning: The one magnetometry candidate whose two disqualifiers for the others are its advantages: diamond is intrinsically radiation-hard (NV centres are CREATED by irradiation+annealing) and NV works in high magnetic field, up to several T. Remaining gaps are sensitivity at reactor stand-off (~0.9 pT/rtHz demonstrated, not fT) and the need for optical access. Conditional, not qualified.

dynamic_range: very wide; ambient to high field
survivability_reasoning: Nanoscale spatial resolution suits ex-situ component/material analysis (e.g. magnetisation in irradiated conductors), not in-vessel equilibrium sensing; radiation-hard host but offline-only. Included to show the deployed-vs-in-loop cut precisely.

radiation_hardness: low: squeezer & quantum optics are lab hardware
survivability_reasoning: The exemplar of a genuinely DEPLOYED sub-shot-noise device: squeezed vacuum runs continuously in Advanced LIGO. But that deployment is in a vibration-isolated observatory, not a reactor; the squeezer optics are not radiation-qualified. A line-of-sight interferometer ARM could stand off, the quantum source cannot go in-vessel. This is the plant's clearest example of Heisenberg-scaling in practice, quarantined as lab-stage FOR FUSION.

radiation_hardness: high: diamond operates in harsh/high-flux fusion fields
survivability_reasoning: Genuinely operated in harsh fusion environments (JET, spallation sources); fast response and radiation tolerance make it in-loop-capable for FLUX monitoring, conditional for spectroscopy (needs 1e4 counts for 1% precision). NOT a quantum-metrology device: included because it is the neutronics twin's real sensor and the honest content of 'advanced neutron detection'.

is_quantum_metrology: no (gas ionization counter; explicitly NOT quantum in the metrology sense)
survivability_reasoning: Mature and robust, but (a) it is NOT a quantum device (AC-33 guard: He-3 proportional counters are classical gas counters, listed only as the program's own detector-market cross-link and the counting-statistics baseline for E11's 1/sqrt(N) rate rule), and (b) He-3 supply is structurally constrained since the 2008 shortage, making it a procurement risk. Kept as baseline, not claimed as a quantum result.

measured_quantity: 2.45 MeV D-D neutron peak (fuel-mix / burn diagnostic)
survivability_reasoning: Spectroscopic separation of the 2.45 MeV D-D line is offline-analysis (statistics-limited; 1% needs ~1e4 counts), not a control-latency measurement. Radiation-hard and fusion-relevant for the twin's residual-D-D channel, but flagged offline-only to keep the in-loop cut honest.
